name: Symbols that moved most
brief:
An end-of-day report lists the symbols whose price moved most. Trade `i` was in `syms[i]` at `px[i]`, in time order. For each symbol take its first and last price; its move is the size of the change, last less first, divided by the first price. A symbol is a mover when its move is at least `pct` per cent, tested exactly: `std::abs(last - first) * 100` is at least `pct * first`. Write `movers(syms, px, pct)`, which returns the movers, largest move first, and symbols with equal moves in alphabetical order.

For trades of VOD at 100, BARC at 250, VOD at 104, AZN at 5000, BARC at 240 and AZN at 5050, with `pct = 2`, VOD and BARC both moved 4% and AZN 1%. The answer is `{"BARC", "VOD"}`.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 10^5$ trades, every price above 0. A symbol traded once has a move of 0.
Equal moves in the tests are exactly equal, so compare them directly.
hint: A `std::map` from symbol to its first and last price keeps one entry per symbol. Record the first price only when the symbol is new.

examples.note: VOD 4/100 and BARC 10/250 tie at 4%; AZN moved 1%.

how: Submit runs 14 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: `seen.find` before `emplace` keeps the first price; `seen[sym] = ...` on every trade would overwrite it.
The move is measured against the first price, so a fall from 100 to 80 is 20%, not 25%.
The sort key is the move, then the symbol, which gives one fixed order whatever order the map holds.

planted.slip: Measures the move against the last price instead of the first.
A move of exactly pct per cent is left out.
Writes the first price on every trade, so first and last are always equal.
Divides the move by the first price before the test, so an exact boundary move falls just short.
Sorts by the move alone, so tied symbols are not kept in alphabetical order.
